exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Actual current UCR evidence supports comparative history/politics/economics, civil-society theory, qualitative and quantitative research, film/media interpretation and art-historical inquiry. Mexican muralism is an explicit topic of Modern Art and Modern Museums; Renaissance Italy includes Americas-facing exchange. These are genuine bounded regional contributions. Native American Histories does not automatically provide Latin American regional history. The complete24course180EC challenge is mechanically feasible, with9advanced courses, but material comparability, additional directions and stopping remain unapproved while the revised external allocation is unresolved.

candidateAssessment.concept: Latin American histories, societies and political economy
candidateAssessment.assessment: A workable internal 180 EC challenge connects comparative modern and imperial history, public policy, economics, qualitative inquiry, Indigenous histories and cultural analysis. Its advanced work remains broad or anchored elsewhere, without a sustained modern Latin American sequence. The final comparator judgment remains pending. Reconsidered against current formal regional/language/research core. This remains a research direction pending the complete revised comparator; neither mechanical infeasibility nor an accepted alternative or final no-match is established.

Psycholinguistics teaches language processing, acquisition and bilingualism, and stylistics analyzes language choices in texts. This does not provide repeated regional work on historical language varieties, contact, migration and identity. No full option is presented pending cohort verification. Reconsidered against current formal regional/language/research core. This remains a research direction pending the complete revised comparator; neither mechanical infeasibility nor an accepted alternative or final no-match is established.

candidateAssessment.concept: Latin American literature, film and popular culture
candidateAssessment.assessment: Film, adaptation and literary analysis offer tools for examining texts and images. Mexican muralism is one genuine regional topic within Modern Art and Modern Museums. Together the courses still center on comparative media and general cultural analysis, without sustained teaching in Latin American literature, film and popular culture. Final comparability remains pending. Reconsidered against current formal regional/language/research core. This remains a research direction pending the complete revised comparator; neither mechanical infeasibility nor an accepted alternative or final no-match is established.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s bachelor in Latin American Studies combines Spanish or Portuguese with the study of Latin American history, politics, languages, literature and film. The degree develops regional research skills. Its language goals are C1 for reading and B2 for listening, speaking and writing. The first-year courses shown here illustrate the Spanish language choice.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The displayed 90 EC comprises the confirmed 60 EC first year and 30 EC of elective space. The allocation and sequence of the remaining 90 required EC for 2026 entrants still need confirmation, including the taught courses around second-year study abroad. A complete comparison with UCR remains unfinished.

curriculum.limitation: Verified subset: 90 of 180 EC. The eight first-year courses total 60 EC; a further 30 EC is elective space. Leiden says 2026 entrants will study abroad in the first semester of year two, while the annual table still uses the earlier second-semester arrangement. The remaining 90 required EC and their sequence await confirmation.

componentNotes.open-elective-space: 30 EC of elective space, which can include a minor, approved courses or a placement. Level and non-overlap rules apply; Honours courses cannot count here.
